title: Recommended settings, by goal
takeaway: Defaults are starting points: choose a goal, make trade-offs explicit, and measure on your workload.

scenes.title: Defaults are not an optimum
scenes.visual: 11.1.1: statCard says no universal preset. 11.1.2: diagram separates shipped defaults from three proposed profile cards. Pin dateStamp and gradeBadge C; profiles remain explicitly conditional, not benchmark winners. 11.1.3: underline defaults versus deliberate deviations.

sentences.text: Choose omp settings around your goal: interactive safety, controlled spending, or more explicit review, rather than searching for one universally best preset.
These profiles combine official guidance with recommendations based on documented behavior; their benefits still need testing on your repository.
Start by comparing each proposed change with the shipped default, so the choice of extra autonomy, work, or oversight is deliberate.

onScreen.text: No universal preset · conditional recommendations, not measured optima · as of 2026-10-08

Shipped omp 18.8.6 defaults: tools.approvalMode: yolo; task.enableLsp: false; task.maxConcurrency: 32; providers.maxInFlightRequests: {}; autolearn.autoContinue: false; advisor.enabled: false; task.showResolvedModelBadge: false · per-call task argument schemaMode: permissive · defaults, not recommendations

scenes.title: Safety-first
scenes.visual: 11.2.1–11.2.2: profile card reveals approval tiers with per-row class and citation. 11.2.3: highlight retained read-only advisor grants. 11.2.4: show observer link and process-local overlay as text/code cards, not an executed command. 11.2.5: child-mode warning remains prominent.

sentences.text: For interactive safety, write mode allows workspace edits but prompts for execution; always-ask also prompts for edits.
Official guidance adds an explicit eval prompt or deny policy when bash restrictions must cover eval’s shell path.
Keep the advisor’s default read-only tools unless you trust broader grants.
Use view-only Collab links for observers and process-local configuration overlays for demonstrations.
Remember that parent approval mode alone does not confine headless children; required prompts can fail their work.

onScreen.text: Behavior-justified · tools.approvalMode: write — reads/writes allowed, execution prompts; always-ask — edits prompt too · not inherited child confinement
Official guidance · tools.approval.eval: prompt (or deny) · bash pattern rules do not cover eval shell execution; headless prompts fail
Official guidance · WATCHDOG.yml advisors[].tools: retain default read, grep, glob and optional recall · do not add mutating grants without trust

Behavior-justified · /collab view — observation, still exposes readable session content
Behavior-justified · --config — process-local overlays, not machine-wide policy edits

scenes.title: Cost-conscious
scenes.visual: 11.3.1: profile card retains worker LSP default. 11.3.2: split task semaphore from provider requests, leave values conditional rather than inventing a universal cap. 11.3.3: diagram routes a follow-up to existing agent; capture-turn toggle stays off. Each row has class and citation. 11.3.4: add no quantified savings caption beneath the separate limits.

sentences.text: For cost-conscious work, keep worker LSP off for search-only assignments, enabling it when the extra navigation is worth the work.
Keep task concurrency finite, and separately cap provider requests according to your provider limits; no optimal universal count is established.
Reuse a context-bearing agent for follow-ups, and leave automatic continuation off when avoiding extra private capture turns is the goal.
These controls bound particular kinds of work; they are not measured promises of lower total spend or better answers.

onScreen.text: Behavior-justified · task.enableLsp: false for search-only workers · shipped default; official schema describes the token trade-off, not measured savings

Behavior-justified · task.maxConcurrency: choose a finite numeric limit; shipped 32 is not an optimum; 0 is unlimited
Behavior-justified · providers.maxInFlightRequests: positive per-provider limits matching your allowance; {} leaves providers uncapped · explanatory notation, not paste-ready YAML

Official guidance · write agent://<id> for retained follow-up
Behavior-justified · autolearn.autoContinue: false — avoid extra autonomous capture turns; separate from memory-backend choice

scenes.title: Max-rigor
scenes.visual: 11.4.1: profile card names exact-selector guidance without recommending a particular model. 11.4.2: timeline shows agent-end strict wait and visible failure exit. 11.4.3: schema gate and explicit nondefault model-badge code card. 11.4.4: cross-family review badge says Low confidence for defect superiority, not source grade.

sentences.text: For rigor, official guidance favors exact provider-qualified selectors when provider identity matters, routed through named roles and agent overrides.
Strict final advisor review can wait without a time limit, so choose it when the review boundary matters more than predictable latency.
Strict schemas protect downstream shape, and visible resolved-model badges expose routing, but neither validates factual claims.
Treat cross-family review as an experiment, not an assurance of superior defect detection.

onScreen.text: Official guidance · modelRoles.<role>: provider/model-id; task.agentModelOverrides.<agent>: "@<role>" · explanatory notation; real YAML uses nested mappings · exact provider identity, not a quality ranking

Official documented pattern · default advisor without a WATCHDOG roster: advisor.enabled: true; advisor.reviewMode: agent-end; advisor.syncBacklog: strict · opt-in; unbounded wall-clock wait, released by failures/abort and documented stop conditions · roster entries configure their own reviewMode and syncBacklog

Behavior-justified · per-call schemaMode: strict — fail after exhausted invalid-output retries; shape only
Behavior-justified · task.showResolvedModelBadge: true — explicit deviation from false default, exposes actual model
Editorial synthesis — cross-family review ablation: Low confidence for superior defect detection · compare equally capable fresh-context reviewers; measure precision, recall, and cost

scenes.title: Measure on your workload
scenes.visual: 11.5.1: diagram returns profile to baseline comparison, recording model/config and separate quality/cost/latency axes. 11.5.2: compare observed benefit against coordination cost. 11.5.3: timeline loops when model or harness changes; settle on the closing instruction.

sentences.text: Compare a strong simple baseline, record model IDs and configuration, and track validated quality, total cost, and elapsed time separately.
Require an observed benefit before paying for additional coordination.
Re-evaluate after model or harness changes, and measure on your workload.

onScreen.text: Editorial synthesis: strong baseline → record model IDs/configuration/date → quality + total cost + latency → re-evaluate after changes
